previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male nursing home resident with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted with fever, hypotension, and leukocytosis. He was diagnosed with sepsis likely from a urinary tract infection and possible pneumonia. He was treated with IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics, including vancomycin and cefepime. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. His infection markers improved, and he was discharged to extended care with plans to follow up with urology for evaluation of a suprapubic catheter to reduce future UTI risk. His chronic conditions, including neuropathic pain and pressure ulcer, were managed throughout the stay.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with tracheostomy, presents with leukocytosis
and diaphoresis.  Question pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior exams most recently ___

FINDINGS:  Single frontal view of the chest demonstrates tracheostomy in
place.  There is a dense retrocardiac opacity and bilateral lung bases which
could represent atelectasis.  Patchy opacities in the left base likely
represent atelectasis although infection should be considered in the
appropriate clinical setting.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is within
normal limits allowing for low lung volumes.  Upper lungs are clear.  Thoracic
aorta is prominent and unfolded.

IMPRESSION:  Patchy left basilar opacity and retrocardiac opacities likely
represent atelectasis although supervening infection must be considered in the
appropriate clinical setting.

PROCEDURE:  ___ tube replacement

CLINICAL INDICATION  ___ man with cracked ___ tube.

PHYSICIANS:  ___ MD(fellow)and ___ MD(attending
physician, who was present and supervising throughout the procedure).

Informed consent for the procedure was obtained from the healthcare proxy
after risks, benefits and potential complications have been discussed.  The
patient was placed on the angiographic table in the supine position.  The skin
of the anterior abdominal wall around the ___ tube insertion site was prepped
and draped in a sterile fashion.

ANESTHESIA:  Topical, 2% lidocaine gel.

Preliminary scout digital spot image demonstrated the existing ___ tube in
adequate position.  Initial attempt to flush the tube with saline was not
successful as the lumen of the existing tube was occluded.  A 0.035 ___
guidewire was advanced into the small bowel wall through the tube without
difficulty and existing tube was removed.  Over the ___ guidewire, a new
___ 14 ___ tube was advanced into the duodenum.  Retention loop was
formed.  Intraluminal placement of the tip in the small bowel was corroborated
by injection of 5 mL of Omnipaque 350 in 50% dilution.

CONCLUSION:  Uncomplicated exchange of a 14 ___ ___ tube over a
guidewire.
